name: Surge
blurb: Coca-Cola's bright green citrus soda of 1996–2003, built to take on Mountain Dew
title: Surge Soda: What Happened to It and Is It Back?
description: Surge was Coca-Cola's green citrus soda, launched in 1996–97 to rival Mountain Dew and dropped in 2003. It returned in 2014 but has been hard to find since.
answer: Surge was a neon-green, caffeinated citrus soda that Coca-Cola introduced in Norway in 1996 and across the US in 1997 as its answer to PepsiCo's Mountain Dew. Sales lagged and Coca-Cola ended production in most markets in 2003. A fan campaign brought it back as an Amazon exclusive in 2014, then to some stores and Burger King drink machines, but by the mid-2020s it was again only patchily available.

body: Surge was bright green, a sweet, fizzy citrus drink with 51 mg of caffeine per 12 ounces, about the same as other American citrus sodas of the time. Coca-Cola's internal name for the project was reportedly "MDK", for Mountain Dew Killer, and the marketing was loud and "extreme", with slogans such as "Feed the Rush" and "A Fully Loaded Citrus Soda".

The drink first appeared in Norway in April 1996 as Urge, which looked more like a pale orange juice drink because local rules did not allow the green coloring. The US launch in early 1997 reached 140 markets with a $50 million campaign.

sections.h: Why it went away, and how it came back
body: Surge never caught Mountain Dew, and sales lagged until Coca-Cola pulled it after about six years. In the gap, nostalgia did the work: a 2011 Facebook campaign grew into an organised push with letter-writing and a billboard addressed to Coca-Cola. When Coke relaunched it in 2014, the company said it was the first time it had revived a discontinued brand because of fan demand and the first time it had sold a product only online.

Only with difficulty. Coca-Cola has not announced a nationwide return, and since the Burger King machines dropped it in 2024 Surge has appeared mostly in limited or regional form; a 2026 report described it as available but "on its last legs". Coca-Cola has not publicly declared it discontinued again.

faq.a: Coca-Cola ended production in most markets in 2003, after launching it in 1996–97. It came back in 2014.

faq.q: Did Surge have more caffeine than Mountain Dew?
faq.a: No. Surge had 51 mg per 12 ounces; Mountain Dew is listed by PepsiCo today at 54 mg per 12 ounces.
No direct replacement was announced. In 2005 Coca-Cola launched Vault, another caffeinated citrus soda, which was sold until 2011.
